explainedBy: Sequence 'hierarchy: control vs service' starts: the CEO points orders down at the worker - the top controlling the bottom, the view the host states.

storyboard.claim: The common view: the top of a hierarchy commands the bottom, like a general and privates.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The CEO in his three-piece suit angrily points at the factory worker in overalls.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Continues 204's CEO dictating orders to factory workers; same two people.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows who commands whom: the boss over the worker.

explainedBy: Same stage, the claim is reversed: the CEO is caught surprised as the other host says real hierarchies grow from the bottom up.

storyboard.claim: In functional systems, hierarchies evolve from the bottom up.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The same CEO and worker; the CEO's pointing stops, his face turns surprised.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same stage; the CEO's angry point becomes a surprised stop.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: the reversal is carried mostly by the callout; the face marks that the command view is being challenged.

explainedBy: Same stage, end state of the reversal: the CEO now talks warmly to the worker - the upper layer serving the lower one, not controlling it.

storyboard.claim: The upper layers exist to serve the purposes of the lower layers, not to control them.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The CEO, now friendly, talks to the worker instead of pointing at him.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same two people; surprised -> happy, point -> talk.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: 'serve' is shown only as a friendly instead of commanding posture.

explainedBy: The body's version: the brain's job is to get food and water for the body - the everyman reaches for the meal.

storyboard.claim: Biologically, the brain's main job is to coordinate resources: finding food and water.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The everyman reaches toward a plate of food.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Moves from the company to the body as the example.
storyboard.addedInformation: Makes 'the brain secures food' a literal action of a person getting food.

explainedBy: Same stage: the everyman takes the drink beside the food - getting food and water is what keeps his cells alive.
noVisual: No icon for body cells; shown through the fed person.

storyboard.claim: The brain does this so the body's autonomous cells can survive and do their jobs.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The everyman, beside the meal, picks up a cup and is content.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same everyman and food icon; reach -> takes the cup, neutral -> happy.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: cells themselves cannot be drawn; the result (the body fed) is shown.

explainedBy: Back to the company stage: the CEO with his briefcase stands by the worker - securing funding and protecting him so he can build the product.

storyboard.claim: A CEO's true purpose is to coordinate the outside world, secure funding and protect the workers.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The CEO holds a briefcase, smiling, next to the worker in overalls.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Returns to the CEO and worker of 205-207; the CEO now carries the briefcase of funding.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the CEO in the service role the narration assigns him.

explainedBy: Same stage turns: the CEO forgets his role and angrily points at the worker - the top micromanaging the bottom.

storyboard.claim: When the top becomes obsessed with power and rigidly micromanages the bottom...
storyboard.concreteVisual: The CEO drops the friendly stance and points angrily at the worker.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same two; happy/briefcase -> angry/pointing.
storyboard.addedInformation: The change from service to control is visible in the CEO's posture.

explainedBy: Micromanaged from the top, the worker slumps: the system gets brittle.

storyboard.claim: The system becomes brittle when the CEO dictates even the worker's hand movements.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The CEO grabs the worker's arm to dictate his exact hand movements: micromanaging the bottom.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same two; the lead shifts to the worker, who slumps under the micromanagement. (fix round 2)
storyboard.addedInformation: Cause -> effect: the control (211) produces the worn-down worker.

explainedBy: Micromanaged, the worker slumps beside the factory: the system loses its self-organizing brilliance.

storyboard.claim: The system loses its self-organizing brilliance.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Micromanaged, the worker slumps beside the factory: the system loses its self-organizing brilliance.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same stage; worried -> sad, the end state. (fix round 2)
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: 'self-organizing' is carried by the callout; the picture shows the bottom layer crushed.

explainedBy: Cause -> effect: one microchip factory losing power for a day breaks the whole global supply chain.

storyboard.claim: A huge, over-optimized supply chain collapses because one tiny microchip factory in Taiwan loses power for a day.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Flow diagram: factory loses power -> supply chain breaks.
storyboard.onScreenText: Factory loses power -> Supply chain breaks
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the brittle company to a brittle global system.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the chain of cause and effect the narration describes.

explainedBy: The factory at the root of the break: the collapse was not a fluke but a failure of resilience.

storyboard.claim: It is not a fluke; it is a failure of resilience and proper hierarchy.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The factory with smoking chimneys, alone on screen.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Names the factory from the 214 chain as the single point of failure.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: the icon shows the factory; 'resilience' is in the callout.

explainedBy: The host turns to the dark side: a system can work too well at exactly the wrong thing - she slumps, uneasy.
noVisual: Abstract framing line with no object; host commentary.

storyboard.claim: The traps: sometimes a system works too well at doing exactly the wrong thing.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The narrator, worried and slumped, on the show stage.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: New section: from hierarchy to system traps.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: pure commentary; the face sets the dark turn.

explainedBy: Same host: the traps are the recurring nightmares that plague societies.

storyboard.claim: These archetypes are the recurring nightmares of systems thinking.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The narrator, now afraid, talking.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same stage; worried -> afraid as she names them nightmares.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: text-carried framing.

explainedBy: The accountant at her desk with the papers, in the mahogany-paneled office.

storyboard.claim: Imagine sitting in a plush mahogany-paneled accountant's office overlooking the city.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The accountant at her desk with the papers, in the mahogany-paneled office.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Opens the success-to-the-successful scene. (fix round 1: bare figure -> named object/diagram)
storyboard.addedInformation: Establishes who and where.

explainedBy: Same office: the accountant holds her glass of sparkling water while the wealthy CEO sits across from her.

storyboard.claim: You sip sparkling water; across from you is a top-1% CEO client.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The accountant with a cup; the white-haired CEO in a three-piece suit enters opposite her.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same office; the CEO joins, the accountant now holds her drink.
storyboard.addedInformation: Introduces the client: the two-person relation of adviser and rich client.

explainedBy: Same office: the CEO, papers in hand, signs away his assets into offshore trusts as the accountant watches.

storyboard.claim: He rapidly signs dense legal papers: moving income, cashing options, shifting assets offshore.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The CEO, smirking, holds the stack of papers; the accountant beside him.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same two; the lead passes to the CEO, now holding the papers.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the deed: the rich man signing the papers.

explainedBy: Same office: the signed papers are designed to dodge his taxes - the success-to-the-successful trap in action.

storyboard.claim: All legal, all designed to avoid his tax burden: the success to the successful trap.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The CEO keeps holding the papers with a knowing smirk.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same stage; the callout names what the papers do.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the purpose of the papers; the smirk marks the edge.

callout.text: The means to compete even more

explainedBy: The mechanism: the winner (the CEO) celebrates, and his reward is the means to win again.

storyboard.claim: Competitive exclusion: winners receive, as reward, the means to compete even more effectively.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The CEO alone, celebrating, smirking.
storyboard.onScreenText: The means to compete even more
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same CEO; from signing papers to celebrating his win.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: the reinforcing loop is in the callout; the diagram follows in 223.

explainedBy: The reinforcing loop drawn: wealth buys better lawyers and political access, which secures more wealth.

storyboard.claim: Wealth buys better lawyers, accountants and political access, which secures more wealth.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Flow diagram: wealth -> better lawyers -> more wealth.
storyboard.onScreenText: Wealth -> Better lawyers -> Rewrite the tax code
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns the CEO's win into the loop it feeds.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the cause -> effect chain behind 'the rich get richer'.

callout.text: A snowball rolling down the hill

explainedBy: The loop's shape: a snowball rolling down the hill grows bigger as it rolls.

storyboard.claim: That is a snowball rolling down the hill.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The snowball icon rolling downhill and growing.
storyboard.onScreenText: A snowball rolling down the hill
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Gives the 223 loop its image: growth that feeds itself.
storyboard.addedInformation: Literal match to the spoken metaphor.

explainedBy: The tragedy of the commons: everyone overgrazes one shared pasture.
noVisual: No pasture or grazing animal in the vocabulary.

storyboard.claim: Other traps: the tragedy of the commons (everyone overgrazes a shared pasture) and policy resistance.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The tragedy of the commons: everyone overgrazes one shared pasture.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Steps back from the CEO to list more traps. (fix round 1: bare figure -> named object/diagram)
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: a list of names; text-carried.

explainedBy: Sequence 'the addiction trap' starts: the everyman at his desk with his coffee cup - the caffeine example of shifting the burden.

storyboard.claim: The addiction trap, called shifting the burden: the caffeine example.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The everyman at his work desk, slumped, a cup in hand.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: New trap; introduces the person and object kept for the whole example.
storyboard.addedInformation: Sets up the caffeine example with the cup on screen.

explainedBy: Same desk: exhausted and underslept, he faces a huge deadline - the clock beside him.

storyboard.claim: You are exhausted, chronically underslept, with a massive deadline.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The everyman slumped and sad, with a clock for the deadline.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same stage; worried -> sad, the clock appears for the deadline.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the problem state: tired person + deadline.

explainedBy: Same desk, the quick fix: he drinks the big iced coffee and it works - he perks up.

storyboard.claim: You drink a 20 oz iced coffee for a quick fix; it works, but doesn't refill your fuel tank.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The everyman, now upright and happy, holding the coffee cup.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same stage; slumped/sad -> energized/happy with the cup.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the fix working: the change of state after the coffee.

explainedBy: Same stage, the result: the coffee only masked the exhaustion signal - he crashes and feels worse than before.

storyboard.claim: Coffee masks the exhaustion signal; you crash and feel worse than before.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The everyman collapsed by his desk.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same everyman; happy -> collapsed.
storyboard.addedInformation: The crash is a visible state change after the high.

explainedBy: Same stage, the loop closes: he grabs the coffee again instead of fixing his lack of sleep.

storyboard.claim: The reflex is more coffee; the burden of the real problem (lack of sleep) has shifted to the coffee.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The worried everyman reaches for and takes the cup again.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same everyman and cup; collapsed -> taking the cup again.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the repeat: the cause of the loop in one action.

explainedBy: The addiction loop: the coffee weakens the natural ability to cope, so you need more coffee.

storyboard.claim: The intervention weakens your natural ability to cope, so you need more of it.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Flow diagram: more coffee -> weaker coping -> more coffee.
storyboard.onScreenText: The intervention -> Weakens coping -> Need more of it
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Abstracts the coffee story of 226-230 into its loop.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the vicious circle as cause -> effect.

explainedBy: Cause -> effect: fertilizer kills the microbes, so the soil needs even more next season.
noVisual: No soil, fertilizer or farm icon in the vocabulary.

storyboard.claim: Same structure: agriculture shifting soil fertility onto chemical fertilizers that kill natural microbes.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Cause -> effect: fertilizer kills the microbes, so the soil needs even more next season.
storyboard.onScreenText: Chemical fertilizers / Kill the natural microbes
storyboard.relationToPrevious: A parallel to the coffee loop in farming. (fix round 1: bare figure -> named object/diagram)
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: text-carried.

explainedBy: The challenge returns to the first trap: the rich man with his wallet, getting richer.

storyboard.claim: A challenge to the success-to-the-successful trap: the rich getting richer.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The CEO holding a wallet, smirking.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Back to the CEO of 218-222.
storyboard.addedInformation: Re-anchors the trap on the rich man.

explainedBy: The CEO with the money: the winner of the market gets the rewards.

storyboard.claim: Isn't it a natural law? If you're smarter, work harder or invent a better product...
storyboard.concreteVisual: The CEO with the money: the winner of the market gets the rewards.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same CEO; holding -> celebrating, smirk -> happy (the challenger's sympathetic framing). (fix round 1: bare figure -> named object/diagram)
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows 'you win' as a person's victory.

explainedBy: Same CEO: in the challenger's view the winner should keep the money as his reward - he holds the coin.

storyboard.claim: You win the market and should get the rewards; fixing it would destroy the incentive to compete.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The happy CEO holding a coin, coin icon beside him.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same CEO; celebrate -> holds his reward.
storyboard.addedInformation: The reward is literal money, endorsed - matching the challenger's argument.

explainedBy: The other host rejects it: it is not a law of nature but a structural loop - the phrase is struck out.

storyboard.claim: It is not an immutable law of nature; it is a structural loop.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The narrator, firm, talking; the rejected phrase struck through.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Rebuttal to 233-235.
storyboard.addedInformation: The strike shows the narrator rejecting the 'natural law' claim.

explainedBy: The loop left unchecked keeps growing until it destroys the society that houses it - the snowball again.

storyboard.claim: Left unchecked, the loop will eventually destroy the society that houses it.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The growing snowball rolling down the hill.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Brings back the snowball of 224: the same loop, now dangerous.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: the snowball shows runaway growth; destruction is in the callout.

explainedBy: The Monopoly game: one player (the CEO) holds all the money while the other player is bankrupted.

storyboard.claim: In Monopoly, if one player gets all the properties and bankrupts everyone, the game ends.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The CEO smirking with the coin; the everyman beside him with nothing.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the snowball to the two players it leaves.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows winner and loser as two people.

explainedBy: Same two: the bankrupt player slumps - no more trade, the game and the economy stop.

storyboard.claim: The economy stops; no more trade; the system eats itself.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The everyman now in front, slumped and sad; the CEO beside him.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same stage; the lead passes to the loser, who slumps.
storyboard.addedInformation: The result of the 238 win: the other player is out.

explainedBy: Introducing balancing loops by law: progressive income taxes.

storyboard.claim: You can fix it with balancing loops: progressive income taxes, inheritance taxes...
storyboard.concreteVisual: The balancing loops that check a monopoly, listed: progressive income taxes, inheritance taxes.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the problem to the remedy. (fix round 2)
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the fix as law made by government.

explainedBy: Same politician, more laws: anti-monopoly laws.

storyboard.claim: Universal public education and rigorous anti-monopoly laws: political hot buttons.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Same list grows: public education and anti-monopoly laws join the balancing loops.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same politician and law; neutral -> worried at 'hot buttons'. (fix round 2)
storyboard.addedInformation: Adds the political tension the narration notes.

explainedBy: Not punishments but checks: the scale weighs the sides back so the runaway loop breaks.

storyboard.claim: These are not moral punishments of the wealthy but checks designed to break the runaway loop.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The balance scale.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Reframes the laws of 240-241 as balancing.
storyboard.addedInformation: Balance = fairness/weighing the sides, the literal role of a check.

explainedBy: Redistributing the means of competition: the everyman gets the coin, everyone stays in the game.

storyboard.claim: They redistribute the means of competition so everyone stays in the game.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Redistributing the means of competition: the everyman gets the coin, everyone stays in the game.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Reverses 239: the bankrupt player is back in. (fix round 1: bare figure -> named object/diagram)
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the before/after against 239's slumped loser.

callout.text: A moral failing of the poor

explainedBy: Same two people: inequality is not a moral failing of the poor.

storyboard.claim: Weakening those laws lets the loop rip the system apart; extreme inequality is not a moral failing of the poor.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Same two people: inequality is not a moral failing of the poor.
storyboard.onScreenText: A moral failing of the poor
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same two; happy -> sad/slumped as the checks are weakened. (fix round 1: bare figure -> named object/diagram)
storyboard.addedInformation: The strike rejects blaming the poor while the picture shows the loser of the loop.

explainedBy: The question of leverage: the politician reaches for the giant lever - where do we push to fix the structure?

storyboard.claim: If the structure is the problem, where do we push to fix it?
storyboard.concreteVisual: The worried politician reaching toward the big iron lever.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Leads into the leverage-points section (246+).
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows 'where to push' as a hand reaching for a lever.
